subject: elephant
pitch: A gentle African elephant calf. Wrinkly slate-grey skin with a dusty, reddish tint from rolling in the dirt, huge fan-shaped ears with a pink flush on the inside, a curious trunk curling forward, stubby baby tusks, long lashes over kind brown eyes, a little tufted tail and round, padded feet with pale toenails.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the elephant calf model using the SDK—sizing it around 1.0-1.1m shoulder height, scaled for a calf, standing on the ground plane facing forward. I'm sketching the skeleton structure with a central body joint and chains for spine, neck, head, and four legs.

Now I'm working out the body geometry using a lofted sweep through stations at the rump, midsection, and chest, each with its own width and height to shape a capsule-like torso, with the joint hierarchy rooted at a central "body" joint.

For the limbs, I'm defining leg chains with hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned symmetrically, tagging them with a "leg" role, and building each chain's path as a polyline through those joint points so the names map correctly to the spans without an extra tip joint. I still need to work out the neck and head placement and mirror the leg setup for the opposite side.

Now I'm sweeping tapered tube geometry along each leg chain to form thick columns, adding cylindrical foot pads with small pale toenail details, and building a curling trunk from head to tip using a tapered sweep along a catmull-rom path through several forward-curving points.

Defining trunk sweep and tapering...

For the ears, I'm planning fan-shaped flat extrusions with outline points defining the shape, positioned sideways on the head so the left ear extrudes toward +X.

Repositioning the ear attachment point so it faces outward from the head, and considering a paint function to shade the inner ear pink where it faces toward the head.

Working out the inner/outer paint logic for each ear...

Now I'm placing the eyes on the head: brown iris spheres with dark pupils positioned near x=±0.13, y=0.93, z=0.5, with a slightly larger white sphere behind for the eye white.

For eyelashes, I'm thinking I'll use thin rods angled upward and outward from the eye edges, fanning four per eye, rather than boxes. For the head shape itself I'm sketching a sphere around radius 0.14 with a slight scale adjustment to give it more depth front-to-back.

For small baby tusks jutting from the lower jaw near the trunk base, I'll use spike primitives with a defined direction and length rather than full cones, giving them a tapered look. I'm now working out the trunk's root position relative to the head center, and placing the eyes on the head's surface using the sphere's radius to calculate the correct depth offset at each eye's x-position.

Next I'm figuring out the tail: a jointed chain of two or three segments sweeping down and back from the rump, tapering in radius, with a small dark tufted sphere attached at the tip bound to the last tail bone. Then I move to lofting the body itself, defining a series of station points along the spine with varying width and height values to shape the torso from front to back.

I'm checking the resulting body height against a typical calf's shoulder height, making sure the legs tuck properly under the body volume rather than poking through it, and confirming the body center and bottom align with where the legs begin. I also want to make sure the body loft is built after the root "body" joint exists so the mesh binds to that bone correctly, since an unweighted path defaults to whichever joint is nearest at creation time.

Now I'm planning the neck and head structure: a short neck chain running from the body front up toward the head position, with the head joint parented to that neck segment and aimed slightly forward and up. I'm weighing whether to keep it simple with the head joint parented directly to the body, versus adding a tapered neck sweep for smoother blending into the head sphere.

I'm making sure no geometry dips below ground level, checking that foot cylinders and ankle joints sit correctly at y=0. Now I'm laying out the four legs with distinct joint names for front-left, front-hind, etc. (hipFL, kneeFL, ankleFL, hipHL, kneeHL, ankleHL), positioning hips, knees, and ankles with the front legs forward in z and the hind legs back, and working out how chain point counts map to joint name counts for each leg segment.

I'm placing the foot pads as small cylinders centered just above ground at each ankle, then adding tiny toenail cylinders angled forward at the front of each foot.

I'm planning to generalize the leg construction into a reusable builder function that takes hip/knee/ankle positions, side, and scale, so I can loop over both front and rear legs symmetrically. For toenails, I'm matching elephant anatomy roughly — four nails on front feet, three on hind feet — spacing them across the toe width.

Now I'm sketching the trunk joint chain as a curving path of points from the head downward and forward, then curling the tip slightly upward to give it that "curious, reaching" look, adjusting the Y/Z coordinates iteratively until the curl feels natural.

I'm defining the trunk as a tapered sweep across these catmull-spline points, parenting the root joint to the head bone, and planning to add wrinkle/scale texture along the surface. Then I'm positioning the tusks near the upper lip, realizing their placement might overlap the trunk's base radius and needing to nudge them outward so they don't intersect.

Now I'm shaping the head geometry as a scaled sphere attached to the head joint, and sketching the ear placement with an extruded disc on the skull's sides, setting thickness and bevel for the rim.

I'm defining the ear outline as a fan of points with slight smoothing for roundness, then extruding it forward with a pink paint rule applied to the inner-facing surface based on normal direction, while keeping the ear positioned slightly outside the head's radius for a natural overlap.

Now I'm working out eye placement and layering: a brown iris sphere, a tiny dark pupil sphere offset slightly forward, and a small white highlight sphere, all positioned relative to the head's spherical surface so they sit flush against it.

Then I'm adding upper eyelashes as thin rods angled outward and upward from the eye's top edge, spacing several of them across with slight offsets for a natural lash spread.

I'm skipping the mouth and lip details for now, and defining a mottled skin paint pattern mixing slate and dusty reddish tones with size and contrast parameters to use across the body.

For wrinkle texture, I'm layering patches on top of the mottled base to create cracked, plate-like skin, giving it that elephant-hide wrinkled look with configurable patch size and gap.

Realizing I can accept Paint values as patch colors themselves, so I can nest mottled patches with dusty red-slate variation inside patches for a richer layered texture.

For other details, I'm setting toenails pale cream, tusks off-white, tail tuft dark brown, and sorting out ear paint as separate from the body patches. For the tail tuft, since calves barely have hair, I'll approximate a sparse tuft using a few thin rods colored dark brown, anchored near the tail tip and fanning out slightly rather than trying to model individual hairs properly.

Working through the sweeps now: the tail gets a tapered radius from thicker at the base to thinner at the tip, legs get a similar tapering sweep, the trunk uses a radius function that narrows gradually toward the tip with rounded caps, and the neck is a simple straight sweep at a fixed radius matching the skin tone. The head is just a sphere, legs tuck into the body at the hips so the tops stay hidden, and I'm now thinking about how to shape the rounded, padded feet.

For the foot pads I'm placing a flattened sphere near the ankle joint, scaling it down vertically so its bottom rests right at ground level and its center sits just above that, positioned slightly forward of the ankle to match the toe area — checking the math so the toenails end up sitting on or just inside the sphere's surface rather than floating above it. I'm also thinking through how many segments the pad sphere needs for a smooth look.

Now I'm sketching out the rest of the build: positioning the rear foot pads, confirming the body loft stations from rump to head cover a sensible range, and setting up the imports and builder configuration (name, detail level, paint sheet size) before writing the helper logic for mirrored left/right parts and the skin texture patches.

For the ear coloring, I'm using a nested paint function that checks surface normal direction to apply pink on the inner ear surface and the regular skin pattern on the outer side, relying on the paint resolver to handle nested color inputs correctly within the ear's local coordinate space.

Now I'm writing the leg-building function, defining joint names dynamically based on side (left/right) and limb type (fore/hind) so the hip, knee, and ankle joints get consistent naming across all four legs.

I'm working out the chain construction for each leg, specifying the joint positions for hip, knee, and ankle, setting the chain's parent to the body joint, and configuring the "leg" role so the contact point defaults to the ankle at the end of the chain. Then I'm adding a sweep geometry along that chain with tapering radius values to shape the leg, followed by a small sphere for the foot pad.

Now I'm adjusting the foot pad's scale and position relative to the ankle bone, then placing toenail cylinders rotated to point forward and positioning them precisely on the curved surface of the foot pad using trigonometry to compute how far forward each nail protrudes based on its height on the sphere.

I'm working out leg joint positions for both front and hind legs — hip, knee, and ankle z-coordinates — and checking that the body loft stations align properly so the belly height sits realistically relative to the hip joints. Then I'm setting up the neck as a joint chain parented to the body, followed by a head joint with its own direction vector and role attribute.

Now I'm sculpting the head itself with a sphere scaled slightly to taper the shape, adding a forehead dome, then building the trunk as a polyline chain with straight segments between key points running down from the head to near the mouth area.

I realize I should swap the polyline for a catmull curve so the trunk flows smoothly instead of looking angular, since catmull returns a proper Path the chain function accepts. For the trunk sweep, I'm tapering the radius from thick at the base to thin at the tip and adding wrinkle patches along its length, then starting to plan the tusks as spikes positioned near the base on either side.

Now I'm defining the spike-based tusks with ivory coloring and explicitly binding them to the head bone so they follow the correct joint, then moving on to building the eyes layer by layer -- sphere for the eye white, iris, pupil, and a small highlight sphere, each nested slightly forward to create depth without clipping through each other.

Next I'm positioning eyelashes as thin rods angled outward and upward from the upper eyelid, then starting on the ear geometry using an extruded outline shape with bevel and smoothing, attaching it to the head bone and working out the outline points that define its curved shape.

I'm calculating the ear's outline coordinates, its depth span relative to the head sphere, and considering scaling down the dimensions since the current span would make the ears overlap the top of the head. I'm also computing the extrusion thickness direction using a cross product of the ear's local axes, then setting up a paint function that colors the ear's inner side pink versus the skin tone based on surface normal direction, differentiating left and right ears.

I'm also sketching out the body and tail structure—setting a chain of points for the tail using a polyline (considering switching to a catmull curve for smoother shape), applying a radius-based sweep for the tail's taper, and checking where the tail attaches relative to the rump's station dimensions.

Now I'm working out the tail tuft: a small cluster of rods extending from the tail's tip, each offset slightly in x and z to create a frayed tip look, colored dark brown and bound to the tail2 bone with a thin radius. I'm also planning the wrinkle/gutter patches on the body using paint, and setting up the final metadata object with name and description, plus the exported build function that returns the baked root. I'm double-checking which imports are actually needed—keeping THREE and the builder utilities I use for patches, paint, and curves, while dropping anything unused like rng since I didn't end up needing randomness.

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy: a root body joint with no parent, a head joint attached to the neck's single named span, and a trunk chain built from five catmull points yielding four named spans without a tip since the name count matches span count exactly. For the legs I'm using straight three-point polylines parented to the body joint, checking that the chain naming logic correctly assigns three names across two spans plus a tip bone.

Then I'm setting up the sweep and loft functions for limbs and body, confirming their options accept radius, color, and station definitions, and checking that bone references for pads, ears, and toenails use the correct joint types. Finally I'm defining color constants and generating mottled texture variations for the hide pattern.

Trunk base sits just inside the head sphere, hanging below the front, which looks right. Now I'm writing out the full module structure with the metadata object and the build function that assembles the elephant calf using the builder's parts, rods, and spikes.

I'm shaping the body with a loft through several stations to get the barrel-like torso, then building the neck as a swept chain connecting to the body, and placing the head joint angled slightly forward and upward off the neck to set up where the trunk and ears will attach.

Now I'm defining the head geometry with a sphere for the skull plus a smaller sphere for the forehead bump, then starting the trunk as a curved chain of joints running from the head down toward the ground, swept into a tapering tube with wrinkle-patterned texture along its length.

Writing leg-building logic...

I'm positioning the front and rear leg chains with hip-knee-ankle joints, sweeping them into tapered tubes, adding footpad spheres and toenail cylinders at the base of each ankle, then checking that the tail chain's span joints land correctly along its catmull curve so the tail-tuft rods attach near the tip. I'm also setting up ear shapes with a pink-inside/skin-outside paint function, placing the eyes, and double-checking that all the color and paint types line up before assembling everything under the root and finalizing the code to return.
